candidates.original_title: Expectations of task demands dissociate working memory and long-term memory systems
candidates.description: Distraction during encoding improves delayed memory performance for complex visual stimuli such as faces
candidates.citation_sentence: The goal of the present study was to replicate a previous study by Zanto et al. (2016) showing a beneficial effect of distraction on delayed memory for complex visual stimuli and to investigate the potential boundary conditions of the benefit – also known as the McCabe effect.
candidates.notes: Experiment 1 tested faces and doors with both picture and math distractors. No McCabe effect found for faces; the door finding was fully explained by extended maintenance duration, not distraction. [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Expectations of task demands dissociate working memory and long-term memory systems
candidates.description: Distraction during encoding of faces improves delayed memory performance compared with encoding without distraction.
candidates.citation_sentence: The goal of the present study was to replicate a previous study by Zanto et al. (2016) showing a beneficial effect of distraction on delayed memory for complex visual stimuli and to investigate the potential boundary conditions of the benefit – also known as the McCabe effect.
candidates.notes: Experiment 1 found the expected delayed-memory benefit only for door stimuli, not faces, and the benefit was attributed to extended encoding time rather than distraction. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Expectations of task demands dissociate working memory and long-term memory systems
candidates.description: Distraction during encoding of faces, presented in blocked task conditions, improves delayed memory performance compared with simple-span encoding.
candidates.citation_sentence: The goal of the present study was to replicate a previous study by Zanto et al. candidates.notes: Experiment 2 reported no delayed-memory difference between simple-span and distraction conditions in either pure or mixed blocks and explicitly stated that it did not replicate Zanto et al. (2016). [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Expectations of task demands dissociate working memory and long-term memory systems
candidates.description: Distraction during encoding of faces improves delayed memory performance compared with simple-span encoding, including under intentional and incidental encoding conditions.
candidates.citation_sentence: The goal of the present study was to replicate a previous study by Zanto et al. (2016) showing a beneficial effect of distraction on delayed memory for complex visual stimuli and to investigate the potential boundary conditions of the benefit – also known as the McCabe effect.
